 November 13, 2026 at 2:44 PM EST Joe Vardon · Senior Writer, NBA No Evan Mobley for Cavs tonight
   Jason Miller / Getty Images The Cavaliers start a back-to-back tonight in Miami, and Evan Mobley is listed as OUT against the Heat with a sprained toe. 
 The play on which he was injured looked like a sprained stomach. In the fourth quarter of Cleveland’s win over the Knicks at Madison Square Garden Wednesday, Mobley got caught in the air and couldn’t land on his feet. He did a belly smack onto the hardwood, or so it appeared. His left big toe also crashed into the court on the fall (imagine a T-bone car crash), and while he stayed in the game, he was complaining about his toe immediately afterwards. 
 We will see if he is able to play Saturday in Cleveland against the Mavericks.
 November 13, 2026 at 2:30 PM EST Sam Amick · Senior Writer, NBA reporting from Golden 1 Center What's Jalen Green's future with the Suns?
   Kelsey Grant / Getty Images When Phoenix owner Mat Ishbia approved the Kevin Durant trade with Houston in the summer of 2025, it was because the Rockets had finally relented on the players that the Suns coveted. And Jalen Green , the No. 2 pick in the 2021 draft who was entering his fifth season at the time, was seen internally as a must-have part of the package.
 “(It) was never gonna get done without Jalen and Dillon (Brooks) in the deal,” Ishbia told me earlier this year. “ Those are the two players we wanted. It wasn’t, ‘Hey, how do we fill a salary with these numbers?’ It was, ‘In order to have Kevin Durant on your team, I want Dillon Brooks to help me with my culture and my identity. I want Jalen Green as a 23-year-old up-and-coming leading scorer.’” 
 They landed Green, of course, but that last part about him heading up their offensive efforts has simply not come to bear for these Suns (5-6). After averaging 21 points per game in his final Rockets season, Green’s scoring dipped to 17.8 in his first season with the Suns (in just 32 games) and currently stands at just 11.8 through his first 10 games (he’s fourth in scoring behind Devin Booker , Miles Bridges and Brooks). In turn, there is a great deal of interest around the league in how Phoenix will handle Green (who has a player option worth $36 million for next season) heading into the deadline.
 The outside belief is that they are motivated to swap Green for a proven point guard. The Suns, according to a team source, insist that they’ll remain patient with their roster and don’t plan to truly engage in trade talks, potentially, until later in the season.

 November 13, 2026 at 2:15 PM EST Jon Krawczynski · Senior Writer, Wolves Jonathan Kuminga has been a surprisingly steady force for Wolves
 Jonathan Kuminga’s line last night: 14 points, eight rebounds, five assists in a blowout win over the Dallas Mavericks. What struck me during the game was how it feels like he's doing this every single night. Terrific defense, rock solid, opportunistic offense and propelling a Wolves win. 
 He's been everything the Wolves could have hoped for and more so far. Heck of a signing.

 The New Orleans Pelicans have ruled Trey Murphy (bilateral patellar tendinopathy), Yves Missi (left knee contusion/bone bruise) and Bryce McGowens (left elbow infection) out for tonight's game versus Memphis.

 November 13, 2026 at 1:45 PM EST Josh Robbins · Senior Writer, Wizards Doug McDermott retiring after 12 NBA seasons
   Steph Chambers / Getty Images Doug McDermott is retiring, the agency that represents him announced on Friday. 
 As an NBA player, McDermott never quite received the notoriety that he earned during his four years at Creighton, where he was an Associated Press First Team All-American for three consecutive years and was the 2013-14 consensus national player of the year. But the level of an NBA player’s notoriety doesn’t necessarily match how successful his career was.
 By any reasonable measure, McDermott enjoyed a successful NBA career. The 11th pick in the 2014 draft, McDermott played 12 NBA seasons for seven teams, appearing in 726 regular-season games and 25 playoff games. He also was a career 41.0 percent shooter from 3-point range, an achievement the vast majority of NBA players would envy.
 After 12 NBA seasons, Doug McDermott is retiring. 
Congrats to Doug on an amazing career! pic.twitter.com/AHX69aOxoN 
— Priority Sports (@PrioritySports) November 13, 2026

 November 13, 2026 at 1:00 PM EST The Athletic NBA Staff Biggest surprises so far: Tyler Kolek (not for that reason) and Thunder injuries
 Tyler Kolek (10-minutes-per-game version) has been a steady presence for the Knicks.   Brad Penner / Imagn Images New York Knicks 
 Tyler Kolek rotation minutes: I didn’t have Kolek playing more than Jose Alvarado on my bingo card to start the season, but here we are. The youngster took advantage of the time Alvarado missed due to injury by being an assist machine and taking care of the ball, and he hasn’t lost his spot. Kolek is even knocking down jumpers here and there, a development that is needed for him to have real staying power in the league. — James L. Edwards III 
 Oklahoma City Thunder 
 How cruel injury luck can be: No contender in recent memory has been struck with this level of injury misfortune. Three starters, two of them potentially out for the season, lost in a single night. The Thunder are handling it as well as possible, 5-4 in games since, but are still playing incredibly unrecognizable lineups and cycling through deep reserves. — Joel Lorenzi

 November 13, 2026 at 12:45 PM EST Sam Amick · Senior Writer, NBA reporting from Golden 1 Center Kings are open for trade business. Could that include Keegan Murray?
   Godofredo A. Vásquez / Getty Images The Sacramento Kings (1-10) are willing to discuss anyone not named Darius Acuff Jr. in trade talks, according to team sources who were granted anonymity to discuss matters about which they are not authorized to speak publicly. 
 With their prized rookie on a historic pace, averaging 26.2 points, 7.3 assists and 3.8 rebounds, this should come as no surprise. The internal excitement over his start has the Kings, quite naturally, pondering ways to speed up their roster reconstruction with the hopes of building around him.
 We’ve been writing and talking for more than a year now about the need for Sacramento to get off the contracts of Domantas Sabonis ($45.4 million this season, $48.6 million next season), Zach LaVine ($48.9 million expiring), and Malik Monk ($20.1 million this season, player option for $21.5 million next season). But those players continue to be a tough sell — at least to this point.
 It’s fair to wonder if teams might show interest in fifth-year forward Keegan Murray, who signed a five-year, $140 million extension just 13 months ago (it kicked in this season). Murray has been ravaged by health issues ever since signing his deal, playing just 23 games last season (left thumb and left ankle injuries) and missing seven of the first 10 games this season (left ankle).
 November 13, 2026 at 12:30 PM EST Sam Amick · Senior Writer, NBA reporting from Golden 1 Center Will bad vibes in New Orleans lead to trades?
 It’s all bad in the Bayou right now, where the New Orleans Pelicans (4-8) have a bevy of talented (and clearly unhappy) players who will surely draw interest as the deadline draws near. Again.
 It was Herb Jones and Trey Murphy III drawing most of the attention from suitors last season, with executive vice president of operations Joe Dumars keeping the price tag so high on them that they wound up staying put. And now, as anyone who has been on social media in this past week has noticed, you can add Dejounte Murray and Jordan Poole to that mix.
 First, it was Poole (who is on an expiring contract) openly campaigning for a reunion with the Warriors. Then Murray (who has a $30.7 million player option for next season) vented on X about the sordid state of affairs before deleting his posts.
 It remains to be seen whether a market will surface for those two, but Murray’s choice to air dirty laundry publicly will most certainly not incentivize potential suitors. 
 November 13, 2026 at 12:15 PM EST Sam Amick · Senior Writer, NBA reporting from Golden 1 Center Orlando is a team to watch as trade season approaches
 With a payroll like this (just $2.5 million below the dreaded second apron threshold), and a playoff track record that hardly justifies the exorbitant cost (three consecutive first-round losses), tough roster choices are coming for Orlando's president of basketball operations, Jeff Weltman . Especially if history repeats itself — or even worse — this time around.
 All of which has rival executives wondering if Anthony Black might eventually be available.
 The 22-year-old guard didn’t come to terms with the Magic on an extension during the summer, and is now on track to be a restricted free agent next offseason. And considering the massive deals already on Orlando’s books, with Franz Wagner , Paolo Banchero , Desmond Bane and Jalen Suggs all making north of $30 million annually on long-term deals, the confusion about how Black’s payday might fit in has heightened the curiosity among his admirers.
 Yet team and league sources with knowledge of the Magic’s thinking pushed back on the idea that Black might ultimately be the odd man out. Depending on what happens from here, the notion of Orlando breaking up its core (outside of Black) if the Magic fall short of expectations again is clearly in play.

 November 13, 2026 at 12:00 PM EST Zach Harper · Staff Writer, NBA How do the Warriors survive Steph Curry's absence?
   Ezra Shaw / Getty Images Let’s say Steph Curry misses about a month with an oblique abdominal tear. That would mean he misses about 10 games. 
 How does Golden State keep pace there? 
 Standout rookie Yaxel Lendeborg will be the key. He’s going to be the top option for a Warriors team that historically falls off a cliff offensively when the 38-year-old Curry leaves the court. Surprisingly, with Curry and Lendeborg sharing the court this season, the Warriors are only plus-1.6 points per 100 possessions. And they have a 117.6 offensive rating (which would rank fifth in the NBA). 
 The Warriors with Lendeborg on the floor this season have a minus-0.5 per 100 possessions and a 113.9 offensive rating. So without Steph, things tend to plummet even when Yaxel is on the court. With Curry on the court, the Warriors are plus-13.2 per 100; that falls to plus-2.3 per 100 without him. Not as dominant, obviously, but still a positive. 
 Replacing or coming close to replicating Curry’s gravity is impossible. What Golden State could do is turn things into defensive battles in the mud, and hope Yaxel and company can score enough points to stay above water. Guys like Brandin Podziemski, De’Anthony Melton and Brandin Williams will hope to fill in some points in the backcourt. But we’re going to see how much the 24-year-old rookie can carry an offense by himself.

 November 13, 2026 at 11:45 AM EST Sam Amick · Senior Writer, NBA reporting from Golden 1 Center Anthony Davis isn't fixing the Wizards. So what's next?
 Anthony Davis has been good, but the Wizards have not.   Trevor Ruszkowski / Imagn Images Anthony Davis tried to quiet the noise about his contract at the team’s media day, saying that he expected to play through this season before discussing his deal with the Wizards “when the season is over.” Yet as our David Aldridge and Josh Robbins reported last month, there is “almost no chance” that there’s a max deal coming his way from Washington.
 Secondly, the Wizards (4-9) haven’t shown the kind of early promise as a group that might mitigate whatever restlessness exists in late-in-life Davis’ basketball soul. He obviously wants the money — and lots of it — but it’s also safe to assume that Davis wants to compete at a high level in whatever chapter might come next.
 To that end, Davis is putting on quite an effective audition for any team that might be pondering making a move on him closer to the deadline. His outing against Detroit on Thursday night was a microcosm of this growing dilemma with the Wizards, as he had 30 points, 15 rebounds and four assists in the double-overtime loss.
 The question from here, of course, is whether teams will emerge that signal a willingness to go big on his next contract before the trade deadline. Add in the fact that his longtime agent is Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul , who has a long history of applying pressure to organizations when he sees fit, and you start to see why there is a fair amount of focus on this situation around the league.

 November 13, 2026 at 11:30 AM EST Josh Robbins · Senior Writer, Wizards AJ Dybantsa learns the shoe is part of the foot
   Getty Images If it didn’t happen in such a tight game, with such significant consequences for the result, a sequence involving AJ Dybantsa during Thursday night’s double-overtime thriller between the Detroit Pistons and Washington Wizards would be remembered as one of the best bloopers of the 2026-27 season so far.
 With the Pistons leading the Wizards 137-134 with 3:06 remaining in the second overtime, Dybantsa caught a pass in the right corner, pushed off his right foot and drove forward, where he appeared to draw a foul on the Pistons’ Daniss Jenkins . There was just one problem: Dybantsa’s right sneaker fell off his foot, and the sneaker went out of bounds with the tips of Dybantsa’s toes still partway in the sneaker. Referee Aaron Smith , who was in perfect officiating position, whistled that Dybantsa was out of bounds before any contact from Jenkins.
 It was a critical play, and Washington’s turnover helped propel Detroit to a 144-140 victory. It remains a great blooper — albeit a blooper with significant consequences.
 Unfortunately, it was the shoes 🤣
AJ Dybantsa was called out of bounds on this play. Although his foot never touched the line, his sneakers (the GT Flight) came off his foot and did touch the line. Refs called him out of bounds. pic.twitter.com/QI0okZZsOY 
— Sneaker News (@SneakerNews) November 13, 2026 
 November 13, 2026 at 11:15 AM EST Sam Amick · Senior Writer, NBA reporting from Golden 1 Center Trading for Kyrie is a light that never goes out 
 Will the Mavericks make Kyrie Irving available before the trade deadline?   Jesse Johnson / Imagn Images Kyrie Irving may not be traded before the deadline, what with the Mavericks (7-5) looking better than expected and their 34-year-old point guard fitting in so well alongside their young franchise centerpiece, 19-year-old Cooper Flagg . Their blowout loss to Minnesota on Thursday night notwithstanding.
 All in all, I’d lean strongly toward Irving staying put at this point.
 Yet when you talk to rival teams about players who would truly change the playoff landscape if they were dealt, and who are widely expected to generate serious interest because of that belief, Irving still tops the list. Never mind that the Mavericks, and Irving for that matter, have shown no signs of wanting a split. Quite the opposite, in fact.

 November 13, 2026 at 10:45 AM EST The Athletic NBA Staff Biggest surprises so far: Cedric Coward and the Heat's lack of defense
 Cedric Coward is looking like the Grizzlies' starting small forward for years to come.   Pete Thomas / Imagn Images Memphis Grizzlies 
 Cedric Coward: “ Ty Jerome , superstar” is the knee-jerk answer, but he at least provided an inkling in his 15 games with Memphis a season ago. Coward turning into a plus-minus god in his second pro season is arguably an even bigger surprise. Memphis is plus-17.4 per 100 possessions when he plays and minus-4.9 when he doesn’t, leading the team in both categories and by far the biggest differential overall. It feels like Memphis can safely plug him in as its starting small forward for the next decade or so. — John Hollinger 
 Miami Heat 
 They can’t defend: Heading into the season, the widely held assumption was that the Heat would be an elite defensive team. That has not been the case. Through 11 games, Miami has been in the bottom 10 of defensive rating the entire season. Things have gotten better in recent games, but it’s still nowhere near the level expected from a team coached by Erik Spoelstra. — E ric Nehm

 November 13, 2026 at 10:15 AM EST Christian Clark · Senior Writer, Mavericks How Garrett Temple ended up on the bench instead of in the classroom
 If Dusty May hadn’t picked up the phone and called last summer, Garrett Temple could be sitting in a contract law course right now.
 Temple, whose 16-year NBA playing career concluded last spring, told The Athletic that he was enrolled in LSU’s law school in his hometown of Baton Rouge, La., and planned to begin taking classes this fall, until May persuaded him to join the Dallas Mavericks coaching staff.
 “We had everything set up to be in Baton Rouge,” Temple said.
 Temple and his wife, Kara, have three small children, ages 6, 4 and 1. The plan was to send them to the same school Temple attended as a child — LSU Laboratory — until the family decided to relocate to Dallas. It wasn’t an easy decision.
 “It needed to be the perfect situation,” said Temple, who played on LSU’s Final Four team in 2006. “Just being honest.”

 November 13, 2026 at 9:45 AM EST The Athletic NBA Staff Are the Lakers real title contenders?
 Luka Dončić has the Lakers off to the NBA's best start   Benny Sieu / Imagn Images By Sam Amick, Law Murray and Dan Woike 
 What’s the ceiling for this Lakers team? Can they finish atop the West and make a legitimate championship run? 
 Woike: I haven’t seen anything happen so far this season that would lead me to believe that the Lakers shouldn’t be considered a serious threat. Assuming health, they have a legit MVP candidate, the most dangerous second option (at least when it comes to putting the ball in the basket), a legit rim threat and wings who can force turnovers and shoot 3s. The Spurs and the Thunder are the standard in the conference, and the Lakers don’t have the full-roster firepower to match either.
 But neither of those teams has Luka Dončić .
 It’s a long year. The schedule has been soft. But the Lakers have played great basketball, and if you ask people around the team, they don’t think they’ve come close to maximizing how they can function as a team. They’re still relatively new to one another in a basketball sense. The defense has to level up, particularly on the glass, but if the Lakers can figure that out, they’ll be tough to beat.
 Read the Lakers roundtable 
 November 13, 2026 at 9:15 AM EST Nick Friedell · Senior Writer, Warriors reporting from Frost Bank Center Jimmy Butler: 'I'm going to play in Santa Cruz'
 Jimmy Butler , who suffered the ACL injury on Jan. 19, proclaimed his desire to experience the G League with a big smile on his face. While his exact return date remains unclear, he is adamant that he will get at least one game with the Santa Cruz Warriors in the NBA's developmental league before returning to action with his NBA teammates.
 "It may not be for long, but I'm going to play in Santa Cruz," he said. "I'm playing in a f---ing game." 
 Butler acknowledged that his former Chicago Bulls teammate and current Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy might not like the plan, but he said he's set on the experience. One person who is on board with Butler's G League desire, however, is Warriors coach Steve Kerr .
 "Oh, hell yeah," Kerr told The Athletic before Wednesday's game against the Houston Rockets. "I love that. Jimmy told you that? I love that. It's funny because I've always thought about that given my baseball fandom; you see these guys go to the minors all the time for a rehab stint and they get several games. It makes perfect sense, but I've never really seen a star player go to the G League. Has it happened?"
